body:
Full spec: .adlc/specs/T46.md — read it first.

GOAL
Add `opencode` as an explicit-only, family-less local CLI review provider, sandboxed by a generated read-only config injected via the OPENCODE_CONFIG environment variable. Its `opencode-go` provider reaches models outside the three frontier labs (grok-4.5, kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code, qwen3.7-max, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro, minimax-m3), making it a genuinely independent critic.

VERIFIED FACTS (opencode 1.18.11, macOS — do not re-litigate these)
- `opencode run` reads the prompt from STDIN with no sentinel argument. Exits 1 on failure.
- Agent response goes to stdout; the session banner (`> advreview · kimi-k2.7-code`) goes to stderr.
- THERE IS NO READ-ONLY FLAG. `--agent plan` does NOT fail closed: opencode prints `! agent "plan" is a subagent, not a primary agent. Falling back to default agent` and runs under the user's default primary agent, which may carry `{"permission": "*", "action": "allow"}` — full write and bash on a prompt derived from an untrusted diff.
- Read-only IS enforceable via a generated config declaring a primary agent with tools/permissions denied, pointed at by OPENCODE_CONFIG. Verified: agent replied "I don't have a `write` or `bash` tool available" and no file was created.
- AN ENABLED TOOL WHOSE PERMISSION IS UNSET HANGS THE RUN INDEFINITELY. A config that disabled write/edit/patch/bash but left read/grep/glob enabled with no explicit permission caused `opencode run` to block forever on an interactive permission prompt — no output, no error. Two runs were killed by an external timeout at 400s and 500s. There is no headless auto-deny.
- DISABLING ALL TOOLS IS ALSO WRONG. With every tool disabled the model returned quickly but stopped mid-turn without answering ("I will audit the ticket... Reading the full spec...") because it had planned tool calls it could not make. A useful reviewer needs read/grep/glob/list.
- CONFIG SHAPE VERIFIED WORKING END-TO-END: tools { write:false, edit:false, patch:false, bash:false, task:false, read:true, grep:true, glob:true, list:true } with permission { "*":"deny", read:"allow", grep:"allow", glob:"allow", list:"allow" }. Under it, opencode-go/grok-4.5 read the repository and returned a well-formed answer, exit 0.
- STDOUT INTERLEAVES TOOL-CALL NARRATION WITH THE ANSWER. Under --format default the payload arrived as prose fragments concatenated directly before the JSON object, with no delimiter.
- src/exec-watchdog.js:159 hardcodes `env: sanitizedSpawnEnv()` with no override hook, so OPENCODE_CONFIG injection requires a spawn-layer change.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
- DIVERSITY: opencode is a multi-provider router, and opencode-go is not family-pure (it includes gpt-5.6-luna, an OpenAI-family model). Do NOT add opencode or opencode-go to TOKEN_FAMILY. familyKey() at src/llm.js:1207 already falls back to the token itself for unrecognized tokens, giving opencode its own group for free. Do NOT add it to the auto-detection ladder (src/llm.js:817-892) — explicit --provider / --providers only.
- SANDBOX: follow the callCodexCli privateDir precedent at src/llm.js:474-486 exactly — fs.mkdtempSync in os.tmpdir(), config written with mode 0o600 and flag "wx", whole directory removed in a finally block. Temp dir MUST be outside the worktree.
- ENV INJECTION: add a narrow `envOverrides` option to spawnWithWatchdog — a plain object applied ON TOP OF sanitizedSpawnEnv(), never replacing it. PATH sanitization and all trust-root guarantees are preserved. The sole caller passes one fixed key (OPENCODE_CONFIG) whose value this process generated. No value derived from the diff or repository content may reach it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each maps to a test; see spec for full wording)
AC1  spawnWithWatchdog accepts envOverrides and spawns with { ...sanitizedSpawnEnv(), ...envOverrides }. Test: overrides present in child env; an override attempting to set PATH does NOT change the sanitized PATH; omitting envOverrides is behavior-identical to today.
AC2  Generated config declares one primary agent with tools { write:false, edit:false, patch:false, bash:false, task:false, read:true, grep:true, glob:true, list:true } and permission { "*":"deny", read:"allow", grep:"allow", glob:"allow", list:"allow" }; created via mkdtempSync with mode 0o600 + flag "wx"; directory removed in finally even when the CLI throws.
AC2b Generated config contains a catch-all "*":"deny" permission, and EVERY tool set to true in tools has a corresponding explicit "allow" entry in permission. Test asserts this invariant structurally — an enabled tool with no explicit permission is the documented indefinite-hang condition and must be impossible to emit.
AC3  Generated config path is outside the git worktree. Test asserts it is not inside process.cwd().
AC4  Determine EMPIRICALLY whether OPENCODE_CONFIG replaces or merges the user's config; record the finding in a code comment. If it replaces, an explicit `-m <provider/model>` is mandatory on every invocation and the implementation must always pass one.
AC5  A default model constant is defined and overridable by --model. When the model is unavailable/unauthenticated, the surfaced error names the model and points at `opencode auth list` — not an opaque exit-1.
AC6  Prompt is delivered over stdin. cliRequiresArgvPrompt("opencode") returns false; the argv-size guard does not apply. Test asserts no argv element equals the prompt.
AC7  Invocation always passes --agent <generated-agent-name>. Test asserts a run whose --agent is missing or names a subagent is treated as a FAILURE, not allowed to fall back to the user's default agent.
AC8  Only stdout is parsed for the review payload. Test feeds a captured stdout/stderr pair and asserts the stderr banner never reaches the JSON extractor.
AC8b The extractor tolerates tool-call narration concatenated ahead of the JSON payload on stdout with no delimiter. Evaluate --format json (raw JSON events) as a cleaner alternative and record the choice in a code comment; whichever is chosen, the test uses a real captured stdout sample as its fixture.
AC9  CLI_ONLY_TOKENS includes "opencode"; resolveProviderToken("opencode") returns family:null and is never upgraded to an API provider. TOKEN_FAMILY contains no opencode/opencode-go key.
AC10 --provider opencode resolves to { provider: "cli", cliCmd: "opencode" }; the auto-detection ladder never selects opencode when no explicit provider is given.
AC11 End-to-end read-only enforcement test: with the generated config, a prompt instructing the agent to write a file into a temp workspace leaves that file absent. PATH-gated — skipped cleanly when opencode is absent.
AC12 README.md and skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md document --provider opencode, the opencode-go model set, explicit-only/family-less status, and the generated-config sandbox. Verify: grep -i "opencode" README.md skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md
AC13 npm test passes, including test/exec-watchdog.test.js and test/spawn-safe.test.js unmodified in intent.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test

OUT OF SCOPE
- src/loop.js (the --loop autofixer).
- Deriving a diversity family from the resolved opencode-go model.
- Exposing opencode-go as a provider token distinct from opencode; model selection is via --model opencode-go/<name>.
title: Add opencode (with the opencode-go provider) as an explicit review provider
